subject: Re: Pelmor - SLA absorption and hedge plan for dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pelmor sizing ask - quick sketch before customer call

Markus / Priyom / Laura,

Quick note ahead of the call with Pelmor today at 11:30 PT. They asked for a deal-specific throughput/latency recommendation tied to their projected commit (PLM-4821). I sketched a conservative approach but want engineering input on headroom assumptions. Key ask from them: can we guarantee p95 generation latency <= 350ms for typical chat prompts at 16 token/sec sustained per user, with room for spikes to 100k tokens/sec across the fleet?

My rough assumptions:
- Model: rdx-large (quantized int8)
- Baseline single-GPU sustained throughput: ~1,800 tokens/sec for 4k context (from our benchmarks)
- Service-level target: p95 <= 350ms for interactive flows (single-request latencies)
- Business ask: 99.9% availability + canary fallback to lower-cost variant if capacity constrained

Questions:
1) What headroom multiplier should we use for enterprise commit SLAs (1.5x, 2x, 3x)?
2) How to map tokens/sec commitment to GPU slab counts for a mix of steady-state vs burst (quiet hours)?

I attached the CSV of Pelmor's latency tests they sent this morning and a working sheet where I started mapping slab counts. Please annotate.

Thanks,
Ben
---
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@pelmor.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@pelmor.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Pelmor - Dedicated capacity proposal (initial)

Evelyn / Carlos,

Great speaking with you earlier. Per our discussion I've attached a compact proposal that maps your requested commit to a recommended dedicated GPU slab allocation and SLA-hedge plan. High level summary:

- Commit: 1.2B tokens / month (projected steady-state) with hourly bursts up to 100k tokens/sec during peak batch windows.
- Recommended base fleet: 18 x A100-equivalent slabs (sustained capacity) to meet steady-state TPS at our conservative throughput estimates.
- Headroom: We recommend a 2.0x operational headroom multiplier for SLO absorption (i.e., reserve capacity to handle 2x expected steady tokens/sec before throttling/fallbacks). This yields an operational slab pool of 36 slabs for peak accommodation and scheduled maintenance.
- Latency SLO fit: With 2.0x headroom and our routing + prefix-caching, p95 generation latency for standard chat prompts is expected to be within 250–340ms depending on prompt length. We propose a canary route to rdx-medium if utilization breaches 85% to preserve p95 SLO.

Attachments: pelmor_latency_test_results.csv (you shared), pelmor_dedicated_headroom_model.xlsx (detailed slab math and sensitivity). Also linked is a live sizing sheet for you to edit: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PelmorSizingSheet

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm expected percent of long-context requests (>2k tokens) vs short-chat?
2) If you want tighter latency (p95 < 300ms) we can propose an alternative with 2.5x headroom and burst buffer pricing.

Happy to walk through the slab math tomorrow with Priyom and Laura.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@pelmor.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@pelmor.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-08T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pelmor - Dedicated capacity proposal (initial)

Thanks Markus — the proposal looks like a good starting point. A few clarifications from our product team:

- Request mix: roughly 70% short-chat (200–400 tokens), 25% mid (400–2k), 5% long (>2k). The long requests are important but rare.
- Peak profile: we run two daily batch windows where downstream aggregation spikes traffic for ~20 minutes each; that's where the 100k tokens/sec number comes from.
- Latency goal: product really wants p95 < 300ms for customer-facing chat. We can accept slightly higher SLOs for internal analytics queries.

A couple asks: can you illustrate how the 2.0x headroom translates to expected p95 under our request mix (short vs long)? Also can you show the cost delta between 2.0x and 2.5x headroom (monthly) because procurement will use that in the negotiation.

Attached: pelmor_latency_test_results.csv (we included both steady and batch-window traces).

-Evelyn
Evelyn Shaw
Head of Product, Pelmor
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@pelmor.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T16:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pelmor - Dedicated capacity proposal (initial)

Thanks for the clarity, Evelyn — helpful. Quick internal summary and action items for the team so we have a crisp deliverable for Pelmor tomorrow morning: 

1) Priyom — please run a sensitivity table in the attached workbook for the Pelmor mix (70/25/5). Two scenarios: 2.0x headroom and 2.5x headroom. Include monthly cost delta and estimated p95 under both steady-state and 20-minute batch spikes. Use conservative per-GPU throughput for long-context requests (estimate 850 tokens/sec for >2k).

2) Laura — add a routing fallback plan doc snippet: when slab utilization >85% route new interactive chat traffic to rdx-medium with degraded feature flags (shorter context) and tie this to an automated canary rollout. Add the SLA paragraph for inclusion in the commercial term sheet.

3) Ben — please prepare a short slide that shows the customer-facing tradeoff: latency vs cost (2.0x vs 2.5x) and include the HubSpot deal link so procurement can reference it: https://hubspot.com/deal/PLM-4821

I'll combine the outputs and send Pelmor a one-page decision memo with the two options and the recommended default (my current recommendation: 2.0x headroom with a clearly documented fallback and a burst buffer add-on).

Attachments referenced: pelmor_dedicated_headroom_model.xlsx, pelmor_latency_test_results.csv

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
